bullets: Game 1 of 7 in a single-deck video (video time 4.3-173.8 s); a win over a Mega Knight / Lightning bridge-spam list (Little Prince, Evo Royal Ghost, Ram Rider, Electro Spirit, Goblins, Evo Giant Snowball). 'Let's go. Beautiful win' (t=171). NOTE: the in-game clock OCR failed for this entire video, so all timestamps are video seconds and no clock times exist.

Ryley names the deck himself: 'we are going to be playing the best Ronin log bait deck in Clash Royale... here we have this log bait Ronin deck here with the wall breakers and with the magic archer. I really enjoy this log bait Ronin deck' (t=6-17).

Offence is always a pair, never a single card: Goblin Barrel plus Wall Breakers at t=38-40, t=75 (called as 'wall breaker split and then Evo barrel'), t=118-131 and t=165-166. The Evolution slot is on the Goblin Barrel ('then Evo barrel', t=76).

Defence is spirits plus Royal Delivery for the first two minutes - the Bomb Tower was held until t=153 and the Ronin was kept in hand for the Little Prince ability (t=69-70) and the Mega Knight (t=99-101) rather than sent at the bridge.

The game swings in one 25-second window (t=118-142): the opponent commits a Mega Knight in the lane opposite the Ronin, Ryley empties his bar to 0 on barrel + Wall Breakers + spirits, his King Tower is activated by the incoming damage and the enemy left tower goes 4858 -> 277. 'What a clean sequence man' (t=143).

Stated cost of the archetype: 'One thing I am scared of with the Ronin though is that it does kind of mess up your card cycle a lot with a lot of different decks' (t=33-37) - the 5-elixir slot is the price of the Mega Knight answer.

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers are the win conditions and the spirits, barrel and Wall Breakers all bait the small spells that answer each other, while the 2.9 average cost keeps the barrel coming back around.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The bait core is unchanged from any Log Bait list - Goblin Barrel plus Wall Breakers, thrown as a pair so one spell cannot answer both, backed by 1-elixir spirits for cycle. What Ronin adds is the one thing bait decks normally lack: a 5-elixir mini-tank that beats the heavy melee cards those decks fold to, which is how Ryley frames the matchup here ("obviously Ronin does really, really well into mega knight", t=29-31). Magic Archer and Bomb Tower cover the ranged and swarm defence the Ronin cannot, and Royal Delivery is the catch-all for anything that gets past them. The deck's damage comes from repetition rather than one big push: in this game the enemy left tower fell from 4858 to 277 across a single 25-second barrel-and-Wall-Breakers sequence played while the opponent committed a Mega Knight in the other lane. The stated weakness is cycle - "it does kind of mess up your card cycle a lot" (t=33-37) - and Ryley's own left tower was ground to 2091 before the swing, so the list can be out-chipped while the expensive cards are stuck in hand.
